score_rationale: Moderate-to-strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 6 major vendors (BookYourData, BizProspex, LeadsPlease, TargetNXT, ITNow Technologies, InfoGlobalData) currently selling hotel and motel contact databases ranging from 25K to 433K+ verified hospitality contacts with pricing from $200-$299.75 for mid-volume lists. Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) hospitality technology vendors (Opera PMS by Oracle, Cloudbeds, Mews, RoomRaccoon, ThinkReservations) selling property management systems, booking engines, channel managers, revenue management systems, and guest experience platforms at $200-$800/month per property depending on room count — hospitality tech vendors pay $5,000-$12,000/year for targeted hotel/motel marketing lists to acquire customers with $2,400-$9,600/year LTV; (2) hotel supply and equipment vendors (bulk amenities suppliers, commercial laundry equipment, furniture and fixtures FF&E, linens and towels, POS systems, key card systems, security cameras) selling to properties with contracts ranging $10,000-$500,000 depending on property size and renovation scope; (3) payment processing and merchant services providers (Shift4, Moneris, CardConnect, Elavon) targeting hotels and motels with credit card processing at 1.5-3.0% per transaction — a 50-room property processing $2M/year in bookings generates $30,000-$60,000/year in processing fees; and (4) travel and hospitality marketing agencies, OTA optimization consultants, and revenue management advisors helping independent hotels and motels compete against chains by optimizing presence on Expedia, Booking.com, and Google Hotel Ads — agencies charge $1,000-$5,000/month retainers. State health departments and licensing divisions maintain public lodging establishment databases: Florida Division of Hotels and Restaurants (myfloridalicense.com) provides downloadable public lodging records by county with facility names, addresses, license numbers, and license status; Massachusetts EOHED maintains public registry of lodging operators (hotels, motels, B&Bs, short-term rentals); Minnesota Department of Health licenses hotels and motels with public lookup. However, not all 50 states provide easily accessible bulk downloads — many require individual lookups or FOIA requests. Zero PII — all business license and facility registration data under state health codes and lodging regulations. Engineering lift is moderate-to-high: state-by-state data harvest from health departments and licensing boards (some states offer downloads like FL, others require scraping or FOIA); deduplication of chain properties vs. independent operators; normalization of license types (hotel, motel, inn, B&B, extended stay). No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell subscriptions or custom lists, leaving a gap for a one-time $99-$149 CSV. Audience size is substantial: 50,000+ licensed hotels and motels nationwide (including independent properties, regional chains, and franchisees), creating a TAM of 5,000+ potential B2B buyers across hospitality tech, supply vendors, payment processors, and marketing agencies. Score is 7 due to validated moderate-to-strong willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors, confirmed partial public data availability (FL, MA, MN confirmed; remaining states require case-by-case assessment), absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, substantial property count (50K+), and four distinct B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior in the hospitality technology and services market. Score is reduced from 8 to 7 due to inconsistent public data accessibility across states (not all states provide bulk downloads or easy scraping) and moderate-to-high engineering complexity for 50-state aggregation.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all licensed hotels, motels, inns, and lodging establishments extracted from state health department public lodging databases and business licensing divisions — public data where accessible without authentication. Each record includes the property name, DBA (doing business as), license number, license status (active, inactive, suspended), property type (hotel, motel, inn, bed & breakfast, extended stay, resort), property address (street, city, state, ZIP), county, phone number (where listed), number of rooms/units, owner or manager name (where publicly listed), and license issue/expiration dates. As of 2026, approximately 50,000+ licensed lodging establishments operate nationwide (excluding short-term vacation rentals and Airbnb-style properties which fall under different regulations). Hospitality technology vendors (Opera PMS by Oracle, Cloudbeds, Mews, RoomRaccoon, ThinkReservations, Hotelogix) pay $5,000-$12,000/year for hotel/motel marketing lists to sell property management systems, booking engines, and revenue management tools at $200-$800/month per property. Hotel supply and equipment vendors (commercial laundry equipment, FF&E furniture suppliers, bulk amenities, POS systems, key card access systems) targeting properties with contracts of $10,000-$500,000 for renovations, upgrades, and equipment replacements. Payment processing and merchant services providers (Shift4, Moneris, CardConnect) targeting independent hotels and motels with credit card processing generating $30,000-$60,000/year in fees for a typical 50-room property processing $2M/year in bookings. Travel and hospitality marketing agencies, OTA optimization consultants, and revenue management advisors charging $1,000-$5,000/month retainers to help independent properties compete with branded chains. A one-time $99-$149 CSV undercuts annual subscription vendors while targeting the same B2B buyer segments.

data_wanted: State health departments and business licensing divisions maintain public lodging establishment databases under health codes and safety regulations. Florida Division of Hotels and Restaurants (www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/) provides downloadable public lodging records by county including facility name, mailing address, facility address, license number, license status, license type (hotel, motel, resort, bed & breakfast, transient apartment), and phone number. Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Economic Development (EOHED) maintains public registry of lodging operators (www.mass.gov/info-details/public-registry-of-lodging-operators) with property names, addresses, and registration certificates for hotels, motels, B&Bs, and short-term rentals. Minnesota Department of Health (MDH) licenses hotels and motels with public lookup. Remaining 47 states maintain similar lodging license databases through state health departments or business licensing divisions, though accessibility varies (some offer bulk downloads, others require individual lookups or FOIA requests). Key fields per lodging license: property name, DBA (doing business as, if different from legal name), license number (format varies by state), license status (active, inactive, suspended, revoked), property type (hotel, motel, inn, bed & breakfast, extended stay, resort, hostel), property address (street, city, state, ZIP), county, phone number (where publicly listed), number of rooms or units, owner name or manager name (where publicly listed), and license issue/expiration dates. Target all active and inactive (but not permanently revoked) licenses. Scope to traditional lodging establishments only — exclude short-term vacation rentals (Airbnb-style) and timeshares (different regulatory categories in most states). Approximately 50,000+ licensed hotels, motels, inns, and B&Bs nationwide as of 2026 (excludes vacation rentals and private home STRs). Target output: 50K rows, one per licensed property. Data is public per state health codes and lodging regulations requiring transparency in licensed facility inspections and compliance status.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and moderate-to-high contract value justification. (1) Hospitality technology vendors: PMS platforms generate $200-$800/month per property in recurring subscription revenue ($2,400-$9,600/year customer LTV); vendors routinely pay $5,000-$12,000/year for targeted hotel/motel marketing lists (confirmed by BizProspex $200 baseline, LeadsPlease $299.75 pricing), making a $149 one-time CSV deliver 33×-80× cost savings. A single acquired PMS customer yields 16×-64× ROI. (2) Hotel supply and equipment vendors: renovation and equipment contracts of $10,000-$500,000 make a $149 prospect database trivial — one signed project yields 67×-3,356× ROI vs. database cost. (3) Payment processing providers: a 50-room property processing $2M/year in bookings generates $30,000-$60,000/year in merchant services fees at 1.5-3.0% — a single acquired hotel yields 201×-402× ROI vs. $149 database, and processors serve properties for 3-5+ years (cumulative $90K-$300K revenue). (4) Marketing agencies: $1,000-$5,000/month retainers ($12,000-$60,000/year per client) make a $149 database negligible — one retained hotel client yields 80×-402× ROI. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $1,000 (all existing vendors sell subscriptions or custom extracts, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with validated commercial pricing from 6+ vendors creates a moderate-strength low-price entry wedge. However, public data inconsistency across states (FL and MA confirmed accessible; remaining 48 states require case-by-case validation) introduces harvest complexity that may increase time-to-ship and reduce margins vs. other opportunities with uniform 50-state public databases (e.g., state bar associations, NMLS).
